title: Proof of uniqueness of the categorical Fourier transform
html:
Proof. Proof of uniqueness of the categorical Fourier transform

The strategy leverages the Peter-Weyl theorem. By requiring the transform to agree with the dual action \mathcal{L}[f](-i \xi) on irreducible components, the representation ring structure uniquely pins down the labels and forces the uniqueness of the monoidal functor \mathcal{F}.

Wick rotation inherits uniqueness from (uniqueness of categorical Laplace transform): \mathcal{F}[f](\xi) = \mathcal{L}[f](-i\xi) for a unique \mathcal{L} gives a unique \mathcal{F}. Independently, the Peter--Weyl decomposition is unique up to permutation of irreducibles (which is a change of labelling, not of the functor).
